summary: Verified seller earning fix: delivery_fee is now added to seller_earning_usd when the shop/restaurant is seller-managed. 8/8 new tests pass, 12/12 iter17 + 16/16 iter18 regression pass, /api/health ok.
critical_code_review_comments: cod.py:436-442 and cod.py:554-560 duplicate the same delivery-managed-by branching logic. Consider extracting into a small helper `_seller_keeps_delivery(entity, sysconf)` to avoid drift between marketplace splits and restaurant orders.

cod.py:429 reuses variable `rate` as commission_rate, while global_rate is derived from sysconf.commission_rate — the naming is a bit misleading (global_rate looks like an FX rate). Consider renaming to `default_commission_rate` for readability.

initialize_restaurant_order_cod does not multiply delivery_fee, but if a shop later switches from seller→admin managed after order creation, the stored seller_earning_usd remains stale. That's correct per spec (immutable at creation) but worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: Session fixture seeds seller, 2 shops (seller/admin managed), 4 restaurants (seller/admin/default/default+CR override), matching menu items and products. All TEST_ prefixed and cleaned in teardown. Tests bind cod module directly with an in-process fake get_settings to toggle admin_manages_delivery + commission_rate per test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter19 verified all 8 problem-statement scenarios (rest seller-managed, admin-managed, default+platform-off, default+platform-on, 10% commission, marketplace seller-managed, marketplace admin-managed) plus health. Approach: import cod module and bind() with fake get_settings — avoids the need to set up admin delivery-pricing rules for full end-to-end POST /api/restaurant-orders. If future changes touch these two functions, extend test_iter19_seller_delivery_earning.py.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature verification, fix implementation is correct.
